content.title: About
content.content: Corn tortilla is a traditional Mexican flatbread made from whole‑grain corn flour (masa harina). Thin, flexible, and slightly sweet, it serves as the base for tacos, burritos, chips and many other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn tortillas originated in Mesoamerica more than 3,000 years ago.
Traditional cooking uses a hot stone griddle called a "comal".
They are naturally gluten‑free, making them suitable for people with celiac disease.
In the United States, corn tortilla consumption surpassed 5 billion pieces per year in the 2020s.
Tortillas can be served soft or become crispy after frying.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Corn flour provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Tortillas deliver slow‑releasing energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6 and niacin
items.content: These B‑vitamins aid protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with wheat tortillas, corn versions typically contain less fat.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for those with gluten intolerance.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Packaged tortillas often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: Glycemic index
items.content: Corn tortillas have a moderate glycemic index, so portion control is advised for diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tortillas as shells for tacos, burritos, quesadillas, or cut them into wedges and fry for crunchy chips. Warm them on a dry skillet, microwave, or grill before filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight bag in a cool, dry place. After opening, store in the refrigerator for up to 7‑10 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
